text: Drop a pinch of salt into water, and it seems to vanish. But where does it go?
Salt is a crystal: sodium and chloride ions, locked together by opposite charges.
Water molecules are tiny magnets of charge: slightly negative at the oxygen, slightly positive at the hydrogens.
At the edges of the crystal, they crowd in, oxygens toward sodium, hydrogens toward chloride, and tug.
One by one, the ions break free, each wrapped in its own shell of water.
That is dissolving: not vanishing, just spreading out, one ion at a time.
